name: Do I need shoe molding if my baseboards already look good?

mainEntity.name: Do I need shoe molding if my baseboards already look good?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shoe molding serves a specific purpose beyond just aesthetics, primarily to cover the expansion gaps necessary for floating floors or inconsistencies where the baseboard meets the floor. Even if your baseboards appear fine, these gaps might be present. The decision factor often hinges on the type of flooring and the desired level of finish. Shoe molding provides a refined, finished edge that can elevate the overall appearance of a room, creating a seamless transition from wall to floor.
acceptedAnswer.description: Shoe molding covers expansion gaps and provides a finished look where baseboards meet the floor, even if baseboards appear good.
